text:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran into a perf regression on Dedicated during the 2pm load run. KV cache hit rate dropped from ~88% -> ~62% and tail latencies spiked. Suspect interaction between SDK cache opt-in header and streaming retry behavior.

ajay: Can you share a short repro or profiler traces?

maria: Pasted the relevant profiler slice below. Notice repeated warmup work for identical prefix keys across retries.

maria: ```
WARMUP start key=prefix:customer/123 seq=0 req_id=abc123 opt_in=true
WARMUP start key=prefix:customer/123 seq=0 req_id=abc123 retry=true
WARMUP duplicate detected? no, starting again -> kernel select: small-batch -> fallback large
cache miss for key=prefix:customer/123 (previously hot) -> backend exec
selected kernel: fused_attention_v2 (higher mem)

Profiler summary: warmup_cpu_ms=18 -> 34 (per duplicate), kv_store_ops=+2x, tail_p95 latency +120ms
```

sophie: ugh. that looks like the SDK is resending the opt-in header on retries and server treats each incoming request as a fresh warmup candidate instead of deduping by client-request-id. we've seen similar before with streaming reconnects.

tyler: Repro with curl (streaming + header):

tyler: ```bash
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'X-Redwood-Cache: optin=1' -H 'X-Client-Request-Id: abc123' \
  -d @- https://api.redwood/infer/stream
# then simulate a transient network glitch and client retries the stream with same request id
```

ajay: Observed behavior: server-side retry path clears transient warmup marker if the request arrives with a retry flag (x-retry=true). SDK currently sets x-retry=true for streaming reconnects but downstream proxies sometimes strip it. So sometimes retries look like brand-new requests with opt-in header present.

maria: That explains the duplicate warmups. Also saw kernel selection flip because the duplicate warmup changed the sequence length histogram seen by the scheduler (small sequences -> big sequences), triggering a different kernel and larger memory footprint.

sophie: Short-term mitigation ideas:
- dedupe warmup by X-Client-Request-Id on server (ignore warmup if warmup for same key+client_id is in progress)
- treat requests with X-Redwood-Cache optin only if accompanied by X-Client-Request-Id (server rejects ambiguous opt-ins)

tyler: Medium-term: make SDK handshake explicit: first POST to /cache/handshake that returns a warmup token; streaming retries must supply token. That decouples opt-in from transient headers.

ajay: Also saw retries sometimes lose the header when proxies buffer; alternative is to move opt-in into the auth token metadata (signed) so it survives proxies.

maria: Proposed quick patch: server-level dedupe key = sha256(client_id + prefix_key + model + warmup_type). If warmup already running, return 202 ack and skip kernel warmup. I can roll a PoC.

sophie: +1. please also add telemetry counters: warmup_deduped, warmup_dup_count, warmup_by_retry_flag. We need graphs.

tyler: I'll open a tiny SDK PR to stop propagating opt-in on automatic retries and to preserve X-Client-Request-Id.

maria: Follow-ups:
- I will push PoC server change behind a feature flag and run canary with loadtest A/B.
- Tyler will send SDK change request and a small integration test for streaming reconnects.
- Ajay will add profiler hooks to capture kernel selection distribution pre/post dedupe.

maria: TL;DR: duplicate warmups caused by unreliable retry header + opt-in header -> KV churn + kernel flip + p95 spike. Short-term dedupe + telemetry, medium-term explicit handshake. :white_check_mark:

runtime-ci-bot: deploy-canary started for feature flag warmup-dedupe on cluster:dedicated-canary
